root_cause.text: In `octep_vf_request_irqs()` the IRQ rollback path in the Octeon VF driver called `free_irq()` with the wrong `dev_id` (`oct` instead of the original `ioq_vector` pointer), so failed MSI-X request unwinding could leave the IRQ action registered and later use freed `ioq_vector` data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the rollback loop from `free_irq(oct->msix_entries[i].vector, oct);` to `free_irq(oct->msix_entries[i].vector, oct->ioq_vector[i]);`, and the CVE description states that `request_irq()` used `ioq_vector` as `dev_id` while the rollback used `oct`, which “may leave the irqaction registered” and cause a use-after-free/crash.

intent_record.how: This makes the IRQ deallocation match the device_id used when the IRQ was originally registered, ensuring the correct handler instance is released during error cleanup and preventing mismatched free_irq() cleanup behavior.

candidates.rationale: This rollback path frees the IRQ using the wrong dev_id (`oct`), instead of the original `ioq_vector` pointer passed when the IRQ was requested. bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable rollback path is present in `octep_vf_request_irqs()`. On IRQ request failure it does `goto ioq_irq_err;` and then unwinds with `free_irq(oct->msix_entries[i].vector, oct);` even though the successful requests earlier used `request_irq(..., ioq_vector)` as the `dev_id` argument: `request_irq(msix_entry->vector, octep_vf_ioq_intr_handler, 0, ioq_vector->name, ioq_vector);`. The mismatch between `oct` and `ioq_vector` means the IRQ action would not be removed correctly. There is no fix in this snippet; the rollback still uses the wrong `dev_id` and therefore does not contain the corrected handling.
